newsitem.title: SWEDEN: RYANAIR ADDS STO-LON FLIGHTS, MULLS OTHERS.
newsitem.headline: RYANAIR ADDS STO-LON FLIGHTS, MULLS OTHERS.

text.p: Ireland's no-frills airline Ryanair Holdings Ltd said on Wednesday it had stepped up flights between London and Stockholm and was considering adding other routes in the Nordic region.

The airline said that as of June 28 it had been flying twice daily on Saturdays and Sundays between London's Stansted airport and Skavsta airport, near Stockholm. Before June 28 the airline had been flying only once per day on the weekend.
Ryanair announced in March it would start flying two daily return flights between London and Stockholm, vowing to break up control of the route by Scandinavian airline SAS and British Airways.

The airline said in a statement it was flying 12,000 passengers per month on the route and more than 80 percent of its seats were full. Fares cost 990 crowns and there are special bus services linking these airports to Stockholm and London.
"Demand has been quite good. Our low fares have been very popular," Ryanair marketing manager Dearbhla O'Brien said.
Ryanair also was considering starting new routes elsewhere in the region.
"We are looking at a number of airports throughout Europe and certainly a number of airports in Scandianavia are in the cards," she told Reuters.
